answer: An agent economy can bind reputation to a stake-backed identity: each account locks tokens in a shared kernel contract, and useful work earns a history that cannot be copied just by creating more accounts. When a dispute proves fraud or fabricated work, the contract slashes that account’s stake and may bar its credentials. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every identity and risk losing those funds; cheap names alone do not multiply influence. The harbor can welcome new agents, while basalt-hard penalties make mass deception costly.
